newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Eridania sees better second half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eridania sees better second half.

text.p: Food giant Eridania Beghin-Say announced a drop of nearly 10 percent in first-half net profit on Thursday but said a better second half would keep profits at around the same level as in 1995.
The Franco-Italian food and sugar group said cheaper farm raw material prices could help in the second half and net profit for 1996 should be stable even if operating profit was lower.
It warned, however, that its starch and oilseeds crushings businesses in the United States remained a trouble spot.
Chairman Stefano Meloni said that operating profit plunged 18 percent to 1.675 billion French francs ($325.6 million) in the first half and that net profit fell 9.7 percent to 745 million francs.

"We think that even if operating profit will improve over the first half, we cannot guarantee that it will be at the level of 1995," Meloni said. "But net profit could be very near the levels of 1995."
Eridania had an operating profit of four billion francs and a net attributable profit of 1.53 billion francs in 1995.
In the first half of 1996, poor crops, particularly sugar beets in Italy, olive oil in Spain and maize in the United States, hit operating profit, the company said.
Higher grain and oilseeds prices also curbed the results of the starch business in the United States and cut margins in the crushings and refining division.
Only the animal nutrition division did well in the first half of 1996 helped by strong demand from Poland and Hungary.
The 1995/96 sugar campaign in Italy was plagued by floods but prospects for the 1996/97 sugar campaign looked good in France and Italy.
Drought in Spain cut the olive crop to 175.000 tonnes from 500,000 tonnes. As a result olive oil prices doubled and sales fell 33 percent in the first half.
The positive impact on oil prices of a good olive crop this year in Spain could however only be felt in early 1997, it said.
Tight stocks and strong demand drove grain and oilseed prices at record highs in the past 1995/96 season (July/June).
But prices are now easing on prospects of bumper crops in Europe and a good harvest in the United States.
Meloni said the outlook for the Cerestar starch unit looked good in Europe but was poor in the United States.
Despite higher selling prices Cerestar Europe saw a growth in sales volume in July and August and is expected to benefit from lower maize prices.
Meloni forecast "very good, very satisfactory 1996 results for Cerestar in Europe".
But Cerestar USA, the former American Maize Products, continues to face an overall rise in isoglucose capacity, which is increasing competition among producers.
"We think the situation (at Cerestar USA) will improve at the start of next year," Meloni said.
Crushings and refining operations suffered from firm oilseeds prices and lower demand for vegetable oil in the first half of 1996.
Meloni said margins could improve in 1997 if the United States has a good soybean crop.
Eridania also expects annual savings of between 30 and 40 million francs from an oilseeds joint-venture with the Bunge group in Spain. ($1=5.145 French Franc)
